body: Cutter Gauthier has done something no NHL player had done before. His hat trick in St. Louis on Nov. 17 was his fourth since Nov. 1, making him the first player in league history with four hat tricks in a single calendar month.
It also stretched his goal streak to 10 straight games, a span in which he has scored 19 times. The Blues won a wild game 8-6, but the night belonged to the 22-year-old.
## Why fans are buying in

The numbers around this run keep getting bigger. Gauthier has 17 goals in November alone and 21 on the season. He is only the third player to put together a 10-game goal streak before turning 23, joining Hall of Famers Babe Dye and Mike Bossy. He also now owns the Ducks record for hat tricks in a season, passing a group that includes Teemu Selanne and Corey Perry.

body: Kirk Cousins picked up right where he left off in Minnesota. Five days after the Vikings traded a 2027 third-round pick to the Raiders to bring him back, Cousins threw two touchdown passes in a 30-10 win over the Packers at Lambeau Field on Nov. 15.
He finished 21 of 31 for 207 yards, and he went 8 for 8 on the fourth-quarter drive that put the game away.
## Why fans are buying in

This is a homecoming with a real story behind it. Cousins played six seasons in Minnesota from 2018 through 2023 and threw for 6,878 yards and 47 touchdowns in his last two years there under Kevin O'Connell. The Vikings had used nine different starting quarterbacks since he left, and his first game back produced a road win in Green Bay. His first touchdown pass was a 38-yarder to Myles Price on third-and-23, and his second went 20 yards to Gavin Bartholomew. Both were the first career touchdown catches for those receivers.

The team around him is rolling, too. The defense sacked Jordan Love eight times, Minnesota's most in a game since 2018, and the win moved the Vikings to 7-2 with a season sweep of the Packers. It was also O'Connell's 50th win, the fastest any Vikings coach has reached that mark.
In our analysis, a familiar quarterback returning to a winning team gives fans an easy reason to bring his jersey back out. That is a popularity signal, not a sales figure.
